method_limits: the arms are three constraints the census row happens to carry; a row whose evidence is wrong narrows the candidates to the wrong node and this study cannot tell -- it measures whether the evidence decides, not whether the evidence is right

an arm that would reject every surviving candidate is refused for that row, so a row can stay ambiguous when its evidence is present but miscalibrated; the refusal is published per row and per arm rather than being silently dropped

candidate identity is (lineno, col_offset) at the face's own cutoff; a file edited since the upstream face was published would shift both sides and the row would be published with no candidate instead of being silently re-located
the text arm compares whitespace-normalised source segments and is therefore blind to two candidates that differ only in line breaks or in quote style

the census's own expr is a re-serialized rendering rather than the source text, so the strict text arm refuses almost every row and the rendered arm carries the text evidence; both arms are published separately so the refusal is not read as absence
the rendered arm drops every apostrophe and every whitespace character before comparing, so two candidates that differ only inside a string literal's spacing are indistinguishable to it
the population is the upstream face's ambiguous rows only; the 255 rows E540 located unambiguously are outside this measurement by construction
population_source: e541_branch_ambiguity.py::population() -- every site of the upstream face whose shape_variants is greater than one, rejoined to the census row that published the same file+line+kind
